channel.title: Empora for WooCommerce — releases
channel.description: Release notes for Empora for WooCommerce, the all-in-one WooCommerce plugin.

item.title: Free download from your dashboard, and corrected pages
item.description: Free accounts can download the plugin from the dashboard, the tools moved to ZTools, and the home and pricing pages now match what the plugin does.
item.content:encoded:
Free accounts can now download Empora for WooCommerce from Downloads on the dashboard, until the plugin is listed on WordPress.org.

  • Our free tools moved to ZTools. Old tool addresses go straight to the same tool there.
  • We corrected the home and pricing pages, which listed things the plugin does not do, including Apple sign-in and a Google Drive export.
  • Pages open faster, and a long store address no longer breaks the store card on a phone.

item.title: An update screen, and policies that match what Empora does
item.description: Empora can now ask you to update when a fix matters. The Privacy and Cookie Policies were corrected against the code, and usage counting is now told once at the foot of your first visit.
item.content:encoded:
When a fix matters, Empora can now ask you to update before you carry on, and tells you why.

An urgent update shows a full screen with the reason and one Update now button. A normal update tells you once, then becomes required the next time you open Empora. Your licences and stores are saved either way.

We also read the Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy against the code and corrected them. The plugin sends no error reports and no administrator email. It sends your licence key, site URL, site name and version numbers.

Empora now counts how it is used by default and says so once, in the bar at the foot of your first visit. Session recording runs only for signed-out visitors on public pages, with text and inputs masked. Your account pages are never recorded, and the Privacy preferences panel is gone.

item.title: Page tours on Downloads, AI drafts and Referrals
item.description: Downloads, AI drafts and Referrals now have their own page tour, so every page of your Empora account has one.
item.content:encoded:
Every page of your Empora account now has a page tour.

Three new tours​

  • Downloads shows the free edition, the premium download for each licence, how to install it, and what Empora holds.
  • AI drafts shows how many drafts your plan leaves you this month, where to ask for a draft, and the Generate draft button.
  • Referrals shows your referral link, how close you are to the next free plan month, and your sign-ups.

Start one with the map button in the header, labelled Take a tour of this page.

Smaller changes​

  • An expired licence now carries an Expired tag in Billing → Licences.

Details: Your Empora Account and Page Tours.

item.title: Your Empora account, redesigned and built for your phone
item.description: The Empora account has a new look on every page, and on a phone it now works like an app, with a bottom bar for Overview, Licences, Stores, AI drafts and More.
item.content:encoded:
Every page of your Empora account has a new look, and on a phone the account now works like an app.

A bar for the pages you use most​

On a phone, a bar along the bottom of the screen holds Overview, Licences, Stores, AI drafts and More. More holds Downloads, Billing, Referrals and Settings, as well as How Empora works, notifications, appearance settings and signing out.

Actions within reach​

Each page's main action, such as Sync every store or Generate draft, sits just above the bar. Dialogs open as sheets from the bottom of the screen, and the page tours run on the phone layout too.

Details: Your Empora Account and Page Tours.

item.title: AI drafts in your Empora account
item.description: A new AI drafts page writes a product description from your notes or answers how a module's settings work, with Speak for voice input.
item.content:encoded:
Your Empora account has a new page, AI drafts, after Stores.

Draft a product description, or ask how a module's settings work. You read every word before it goes anywhere.

  • Product description turns rough notes into a description you can paste into WooCommerce.
  • Help with module settings answers how to set up one of Empora's modules, in short steps.
  • Speak fills the box from your voice, through your browser's own speech recognition.

Each plan includes a number of drafts a month, shown at the top of the page. Details: AI Drafts in Your Empora Account.

item.title: Tour hints follow your account, and How Empora works from the home page
item.description: The one-line tour offer now shows once for your account on every device, and the home page links straight to the How Empora works walkthrough.
item.content:encoded:
The page tours now remember you, not just the device you used.

One offer per page, on every device​

The first time you open Overview, License, Stores, Billing or Settings, one line offers that page's tour. Once your account has seen it, it counts as seen on every device you sign in on. The map button in the header still starts the tour whenever you like.

How Empora works, from the home page​

The home page now has a third button, See how Empora works, after Get started and Explore features. It opens How Empora works, six screens of the account, one step at a time, before you sign in.

Details: Your Empora Account and Page Tours.

item.title: Page tours in your account, and a How Empora works walkthrough
item.description: Overview, License, Stores, Billing and Settings now have a page tour behind a map button in the header, and How Empora works shows six screens of the account one step at a time.
item.content:encoded:
Your Empora account now shows you around itself.

A tour on every page​

Overview, License, Stores, Billing and Settings each have a map button in the header. It walks you through the page you are on, one highlighted area at a time. You can skip it, close it or jump to any step, and the button starts it again whenever you like. On a phone the steps open in a sheet at the bottom of the screen.

How Empora works​

How Empora works shows six screens of the account, one step at a time, before you sign in. It ends on Open your dashboard.

Details: Your Empora Account and Page Tours.

item.title: Bundle contents, paying from a balance on the Checkout block, and overpaid orders
item.description: The Bundles editor now builds a bundle's contents and where it is shown, customers can pay from store credit and wallet on the Checkout block, and an order edited to charge less can return the difference.
item.content:encoded:
Three things changed in the plugin since the last update here, and the reference pages now describe them.

Bundle contents in the Bundles editor​

The bundle dialog builds the whole bundle: up to 50 items, each with its product, its variation when the product is variable, default, minimum and maximum quantities, an optional item discount and an optional switch. You also choose the product pages that show the offer. Saving checks everything at once and points at each problem. See Product Bundles.

Paying from a balance on the Checkout block​

Store credit and wallet money can now pay part or all of an order on the Checkout block as well as the classic checkout. Store credit is used first, then the wallet, and when the balance covers the order no payment method is needed. See Wallet → Spending at checkout.

Overpaid orders​

When an order paid partly from a balance is edited to charge less, the order screen shows the overpaid amount and returns it to the customer's balance in one step. See Wallet → Overpaid orders.

item.title: Documentation corrections — all 78 modules, and the new plan limits
item.description: Three modules were documented as unavailable in 1.0 after they had already been enabled. That is corrected across the site, along with the free, Starter and Professional record limits.
item.content:encoded:
This site said three modules could not be enabled in version 1.0. That stopped being true when they were registered, and the pages were not updated with them. Corrected today, along with the plan limits.

All 78 modules register​

inventory (Advanced Inventory Management), livechat (Live Chat & Customer Support) and store_credit (Store Credit & Wallet) were described across this site as being in the catalogue but impossible to switch on. They were registered on 2 September, and the documentation kept saying otherwise.

Every one of the 78 modules in the plugin's manifest registers and can be enabled. The only thing deciding whether you can switch a module on is whether your plan includes it.

The three modules' reference pages were rewritten from the code they actually run, rather than described as unreleased work:

  • Advanced Inventory Management — stock per location, transfers with their own lifecycle, an audit log, and the daily low-stock alert.
  • Live Chat & Customer Support — the storefront widget, the agent roster, session assignment and transfer, and message polling.
  • Store Credit & Wallet — the issued-credit ledger, and how it sits beside Wallet.

Wallet and Store Credit are two ledgers, not two versions of one feature​

Documentation that treated Store Credit as a dropped duplicate of Wallet was wrong about what the two modules are for. Wallet holds money the customer paid in; Store Credit holds value the store issued — goodwill, compensation, the value of a return. They keep separate ledgers because they are not the same money. At checkout the customer sees one combined balance, and the issued credit is spent first, because it is the store's own liability and it can expire.

Free, Starter and Professional no longer cap records​

The product limits on how many products, orders and customers Empora's modules will process have been removed from the Free, Starter and Professional plans. All five tiers are now unlimited on those three counts.

Prices, site counts and module counts are unchanged: Free $0 (1 site, 7 modules), Starter $19 (27 modules), Professional $49 (48 modules), Business $99 (3 sites, 68 modules), Enterprise $299 (unlimited sites, all 78). Import and export allowances are unchanged too — they remain the practical difference between the tiers. See Plans & pricing.

Also corrected​

  • The modules overview listed module names that no longer exist beside their replacements, and claimed the plugin carried "90+ module directories". It now lists the 78 real modules by area, with the key each one uses.
  • The referral program page said neither reward type had anything listening for it, so no payout was ever delivered. Both types now have a listener, and a referral is marked paid only once delivery is confirmed. A store-credit reward is credited to the customer's wallet, so it needs the Wallet module enabled.
  • llms.txt, which is what AI assistants read, carried the same false module claim and the old plan limits.

item.title: 1.0.0 — in preparation
item.description: Empora for WooCommerce 1.0.0 has not been released yet. What the first release contains, and what this changelog will carry once it ships.
item.content:encoded:
Empora for WooCommerce 1.0.0 has not been released yet. No version has been published to WordPress.org, to CodeCanyon, or to the Play Store. This page is the changelog those releases will appear in, and this first entry records what 1.0.0 contains so the documentation and the software describe the same thing when it ships.

What 1.0.0 contains​

78 modules, each independently switchable, all of which register and are usable in this version. Seven of them are the free core and need no license: Product Filters, Reviews Enhancement, Wishlist, Product Compare, Social Media Integration, SEO & Schema Markup, and Dynamic Pricing. The rest are unlocked by a plan. The full list, with the plan each module belongs to, is the module reference.

One admin surface. A single Empora menu in WordPress admin holding the Modules grid, a unified Settings store, a Dashboard reporting license and module status, and Reports.

HPOS compatibility. Empora declares compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage and reads orders through the WooCommerce order APIs rather than querying post tables directly, so it runs on stores that have made the switch.

Plans that the software enforces. Five tiers — Free, Starter, Professional, Business and Enterprise — with per-plan module sets, site counts and record limits. See Plans & pricing.

What 1.0.0 does not contain​

Being specific about this matters more than the feature list:

  • No self-serve purchase. No payment provider ships in 1.0, so there is no checkout. Paid plans are arranged by contacting the author. The plans themselves are real and enforced.
  • No WordPress.org listing yet. Installation is by uploading the plugin ZIP — see Installation.

Requirements​

WordPress 6.2 or newer, WooCommerce 8.0 or newer, PHP 8.1 or newer. Details and hosting notes are in Requirements & compatibility.

Subscribing​

This changelog publishes an RSS feed. Subscribe to it if you want release notes without checking back.
